title: `deleteAudit()` hard-deletes scope items without checking open findings or CARs — orphaned records corrupt reports
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/controllers/audit-assurance.controller.js:598–612`

Root Cause: `deleteAudit()` deletes the audit and scope items but does not cascade to `audit_findings` or `audit_nonconformances`. These records remain with a dangling `auditId` reference.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-002 in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/controllers/audit-assurance.controller.js lines 598–612.

deleteAudit() leaves orphaned findings, NCs, and CARs.

Required changes:
1. Pre-delete check:
     const [findingCount, ncCount, carCount] = await Promise.all([
       AuditFinding.countDocuments({ auditId, isDeleted: { $ne: true } }),
       AuditNonConformance.countDocuments({ auditId, deletedAt: null }),
       CorrectiveAction.countDocuments({ auditId, status: { $nin: ['closed', 'cancelled'] } })
     ]);
2. If any exist, reject 422: "Cannot delete audit with open findings, NCs, or CARs."
3. If permitted (draft only), use a transaction to soft-delete in order: scope items → findings → NCs → audit document.
4. Never hard-delete audit records that have associated findings.
```

title: Mixed soft-delete pattern: `audit_scope_items` uses both `isDeleted` AND `deletedAt`; `audit_findings` uses `isDeleted`; `audit_nonconformances` uses `deletedAt`; controllers filter inconsistently — deleted records leak
description:
Files: `audit-scope-item.model.js` (isDeleted+deletedAt), `audit-finding.model.js` (isDeleted), `audit-nonconformance.model.js` (deletedAt)

Root Cause: Three different soft-delete conventions are used across the module. Controllers filter inconsistently, causing deleted records to appear in some query results.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-003 across audit-assurance models and controllers.

Three different soft-delete conventions cause deleted records to leak into results.

Standardise to deletedAt: Date (null = active, Date = deleted):
1. audit-scope-item.model.js: add deletedAt: { type: Date, default: null }. If isDeleted exists, add a pre-save hook: if (this.isDeleted && !this.deletedAt) this.deletedAt = new Date().
2. audit-finding.model.js: same.
3. audit-nonconformance.model.js: already uses deletedAt — verify all queries filter on it.
4. Add a Mongoose plugin or default query filter on each model: schema.pre(/^find/, function() { if (!this.getQuery().includeDeleted) this.where({ deletedAt: null }); }).
5. Audit every controller query to confirm consistent filtering.
```
fixEvidence: `audit-nonconformance.model.js` standardised to `deletedAt`; `audit-finding.model.js` retains both `isDeleted` AND `deletedAt` with sync middleware — partial fix only

title: Closure approve/reject protected by `audit.update` (too broad) — no `audit.approve` permission; any write-access user can approve their own closure
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/routes/audit-closure.routes.js:16–17`

Root Cause: Approve and reject closure routes use `requirePermission('audit.update')`. The lead auditor who submitted the closure also holds `audit.update`, enabling self-approval. ISO 27001 requires independent review.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-004 in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/routes/audit-closure.routes.js lines 16–17.

Closure approval uses audit.update — submitting auditor can approve their own closure.

Required changes:
1. Create permission: audit.approve_closure.
2. Update approve/reject routes to requirePermission('audit.approve_closure').
3. In approveClosure() service, add independence check:
     if (closure.submittedBy.toString() === userId.toString())
       throw createError(403, 'You cannot approve a closure you submitted.');
4. Assign audit.approve_closure only to Audit Manager and Admin roles — not Lead Auditor.
5. Document permission matrix in the routes directory.
```

title: Closure state transitions not enforced — `not_started → pending_approval` bypasses checklist; `rejected → approved` without rework cycle
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/services/audit-closure.service.js:52–202`

Root Cause: The closure lifecycle (`not_started → in_progress → pending_approval → approved/rejected → closed`) has no state machine. `rejected → approved` is possible without a rework cycle.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-006 in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/services/audit-closure.service.js lines 52–202.

Closure transitions are not validated — rejected can go directly to approved.

Required changes:
1. Define transition map:
     const CLOSURE_TRANSITIONS = {
       not_started: ['in_progress'],
       in_progress: ['pending_approval'],
       pending_approval: ['approved', 'rejected'],
       rejected: ['in_progress'],
       approved: ['closed'],
       closed: []
     };
2. Validate every status update against this map; throw 422 on invalid transition.
3. Rejection must require rejectionReason (throw 400 if missing) and record who rejected and when.
4. Return to in_progress after rejection must require updatedChecklistNotes documenting what was reworked.
```
